title: 5K Training - No Boundaries
location: Montclair - Anderson Park, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class.

Click here to register for the early bird price, available until April 3rd.

Click here for registrations April 3rd and later.

Have you always wanted to run or walk a 5K but didn't know how to begin training? Maybe you are nervous or don't want to do it alone? Maybe you have had a hard time sticking to a training program in the past? If you answered "Yes" to any of the above, our iconic beginner program is perfect for you. title: Bank of America Museums on Us Weekend
location: NJ
description:
BANK OF AMERICA MUSEUMS ON US® OFFERS FREE ADMISSION JUNE 6th & 7th 
WHAT: Bank of America, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank cardholders can receive FREE general admission to cultural attractions across New York City and New Jersey on Saturday and Sunday. 
WHEN: Saturday, June 6th & Sunday, June 7th (+ the first full weekend of each month) 
WHERE: Learn something new this month with a visit to a participating cultural institution, including:
Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum, 2 East 91st Street, New York, NY 10128
The Intrepid Museum, Pier 86 W 46th, New York, NY 10036
The Jewish Museum, 1109 5th Ave, New York, NY 10128 (Sundays only)

The Metropolitan Museum of Art – The Met Fifth Avenue, 1000 5th Ave, New York, NY 10028

Liberty Science Center, 222 Jersey City Boulevard, Jersey City, NJ 07305
Montclair Art Museum, 3 South Mountain Ave., Montclair, NJ 07042
Morris Museum, 6 Normandy Heights Road, Morristown, NJ 07960
The Newark Museum of Art, 49 Washington Street, Newark, NJ 07102

WHY: Bank of America believes the arts have a unique ability to connect people and communities and help local economies thrive. This is one example of how the bank strengthens the local communities it serves in, creates greater cultural understanding, and expands accessibility to the arts.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
**IMPORTANT NOTE:** In order to prevent event cancellation I’m going to need at least one member who I’ve previously met and played with to confirm meeting at 8 AM via public comment. Not everyone is going to want to start this early but no one is going to want to hold a court by themselves for a half an hour or more. So when lacking this confirmation I’m going to cancel the event within an hour of the official start time. Either way, please use the comments to coordinate better start times for yourselves with others. We can’t please everyone with an exact start time but if we all communicate here then we can at least try. So please let us know your planned arrival time in the comments and be sure to monitor the event and discussion and be ready to adapt accordingly.

**VOTES:** Since this is still a “test” time slot, I welcome votes from proven members for changing the official start time. If we’ve already met then private message me your vote for the exact time and I’ll start an official record. Thanks for your patience and understanding as we work this all out.

**ABOUT THE GROUP:** We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition. We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

description:
Paper shredded at the event will be recycled. There is no limit on how much paper residents may bring to the Paper Shredding Day. The Essex County Paper Shredding Day is for Essex County residents only. Residents are not charged when they bring materials, but they must provide proof of residency at the site. Commercial businesses may not drop off materials. For more information, please call the Essex County Department of Public Works at 973-226-8500, Ext. 3001.

title: Roses to Rock Gardens Guest Speaker: Evan Ralph
description:
Roses to Rock Gardens Guest Speaker: Evan Ralph, President of Back to Nature Home & Garden 
Saturday, June 6, 9:30 AM 
 
Have you seen these signs at aspirational gardens in the area? Learn from the award-winning landscape architect behind the firm, Evan Ralph. He will share his vision and process in his talk “From Desk to Dirt: How the Design, Build and Maintenance process come together to create exceptional gardens.” 
This $15 ticket is sold separately at the ticket link and includes a light continental breakfast. Start your day with fresh garden ideas and inspiration! 
 
About Evan Ralph: 
Evan is driven by a passion for outdoor living and a deep-rooted commitment to environmental stewardship. Over the past 11 years
at Back to Nature Home & Garden, he has grown from a Landscape Designer to President, guiding the company’s evolution with
creativity, hands-on leadership, and a relentless focus on quality.
An educator at heart, he’s always ready with a pair of pruners and a willingness to teach—demonstrating what true horticulture looks
like in action. Whether he’s leading a team or tending to his own garden, his motto remains the same: “Garden, every day.” 
Back to Nature Home & Garden  
A design/build landscape architecture firm serving New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut. 
What makes Back to Nature unique is all the different offerings that we have. We’re landscape architects, we’re landscape contractors and we’re also landscape maintenance. We see opportunities where others see challenges. We design and build customized outdoor spaces that are not only beautiful, but are ecologically friendly. 
The Roses to Rock Gardens tour runs Friday, June 5 and Saturday, June 6 from 11 AM to 4 PM
Begin at Van Vleck House & Gardens to check in and get your tour materials.

title: Walk at Grover Cleveland Park
description:
Let's Walk!!
**MEETING TIME 10 AM**

We will meet near the fishing pond entrance of the park, close to Brookside Avenue and the boat house/restrooms.
**GPS location: 138 Brookside Ave, Caldwell. Park on the street.**

We will walk for about 60-90 minutes at about a 3 miles/hour pace. The park has a paved path loop that is a little more than a mile. Stay for as many loops as you like.

Grover Cleveland Park in Caldwell/Essex Fells celebrated its centennial in 2013. As the first county park in western Essex County, the site was originally selected for its natural beauty and its potential to provide a space for relaxation and recreation. It contains gentle rolling hills, broad meadows and other environmentally aesthetic features

location: RecRoom, 1 Lackawanna Plaza, Ste. 6, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required 
Community Sponsorship:
20% of seats are reserved for community sponsorship. Families interested in sponsored spots can email info@kineticmindscreative.com
for details.

Through storytelling, she seeks to foster empathy, bridge generations, and build understanding across cultures.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
**IMPORTANT NOTE:** In order to prevent event cancellation I’m going to need at least one member who I’ve previously met and played with to confirm meeting at 8 AM via public comment. Not everyone is going to want to start this early but no one is going to want to hold a court by themselves for a half an hour or more. So when lacking this confirmation I’m going to cancel the event within an hour of the official start time. Either way, please use the comments to coordinate better start times for yourselves with others. We can’t please everyone with an exact start time but if we all communicate here then we can at least try. So please let us know your planned arrival time in the comments and be sure to monitor the event and discussion and be ready to adapt accordingly.

**VOTES:** Since this is still a “test” time slot, I welcome votes from proven members for changing the official start time. If we’ve already met then private message me your vote for the exact time and I’ll start an official record. Thanks for your patience and understanding as we work this all out.

**ABOUT THE GROUP:** We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition. We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: NY Ridge, Valley, Lake and Rail Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this very diverse hike featuring totally different types of areas in the Orange County NY area!
This time, we will meet at our end point, Fancher Davidge Park, and shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to the beginning. There is extremely limited parking area the beginning, so everyone should try to be at the posted meet point.
The hike will start with a lovely walk on the Shawangunk Ridge Trail, which is entirely on the old Erie Railroad main line at this point for almost five miles.
The line ascends the flank of Shawangunk Ridge, and so the rail bed affords some views along the way.
We will walk into Otisville, where we can stop at Mick's Deli.
We continue through a couple of cemeteries, past two schools and through Mt Hope Town Park and pass another cafe.
Next, we have 2.5 mils on road we must do to reach the Middletown Reservoir trail system. From here, we have over five more miles of hiking off road we will do across the preserve to reach Middletown A short road walk and rail bed leads us to the end.
Distance will be 15 miles. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day
description:

**TRAIL WORK** **CHANGE OF VENUEl** We will **not continue** rerouting the Hogenauer Trail this month as there is an urgent need to create a short-term Lenape Trail entrance from Glen Ave. to the Locust Grove picnic area. This detour is needed now as the parking lot will be closed from June 15th to August 20th for a Green Acres-Open Space grant renovating the parking lot, Fairy Trail and River Road. Wear long pants due to ticks and poison ivy where we will be working. **MEET AT:** Locust Grove parking lot, 197 Glen Ave., Millburn. (Parking in the commuter lot across Glen Ave. -- free on weekends -- may be necessary.)

Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants should wear long pants due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Again, wear long pants due to ticks and poison ivy in the area.

title: Bethlehem Fair Trade Artisans Sale After Worship
location: Assembly Room
description:
Please join us in the Assembly Room on Sunday, June 7th after worship for a sale of select items handcrafted by the Bethlehem Fair Trade Artisans (BFTA), including sandals and olive wood creches, keepsake boxes, and cheeseboards.  BFTA (https://bethlehemfairtrade.org/) is a non-profit NGO, established in 2009, that aims to improve the lives of Palestians by connecting marginalized Palestinian artisans – mostly women – with a larger market for their products. Their work is essential to the life of the community, especially in the wake of settler violence which has cut off the tourist trade and other sources of income. 
The suggested donation for each item reflects a deep discount. You are also welcome to donate what you wish. You can pay with cash or use the QR code available at our table. 
Other items, including textiles, glass, ceramics, pottery, and soaps can be purchased directly through BFTA’s website: https://bethlehemfairtrade.org/

title: The Juneteenth Cookbook: Alliah Agostini - Author Visit & Craft (  Tobias the Horse on the Lawn!)
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium
description:
Alliah Agostini - 4-5 p.m.

Prolific Children’s author Alliah L. Agostini reads excerpts from her stunning kids’ recipe book The Juneteenth Cookbook. She’ll go over the importance of African-American culinary traditions and why great cuisine and Juneteenth go hand-in-hand. Afterwards, kids will make their own 90’s inspired African medallion necklaces - just like in the Juneteenth Cookbook! Registration recommended for reminders and updates. 

Tobias the Horse also continues his tradition of appearing at annual Juneteenth events. Look for him on the Library lawn (Plymouth Street) and say hello between 3 to 4 pm! Tobias the Horse is graciously sponsored by Montclair Township Councilor Aminah Toler.

 

The Juneteenth Cookbook Family Challenge 

There’s nothing like families cooking together! Which is why we’re inviting children and their families to take up the Juneteenth Cookbook Family Challenge from June 1-30. Alliah L. Agostini and The Quarto Group Books have graciously granted permission to share recipes from The Juneteenth Cookbook. Kids, families, are invited to cook up any or all of the recipe items in celebration of Juneteenth. Just click the recipe links below, get cooking, and have your grownups share your creation on social media. Be sure to tag @alliago @montclairpubliclibrary and #juneteenthcookbookchallenge to join our virtual cookout!

Try to make any or all of these below recipes*:




	Jubilee Tea
	Saucy Pulled Chicken Sliders with Bangin’ Barbeque Sauce
	Red Velvet Ice Cream Sandwiches


*Excerpt © 2024 from The Juneteenth Cookbook by Alliah L. Agostini, Taffy Elrod, and Sawyer Cloud. Reproduced by permission of the publisher, becker&mayer! kids, an imprint of The Quarto Group, New York, NY.

Relive the golden age of musical theatre through beloved classics and timeless melodies by legendary composers such as Rodgers and Hammerstein, Lerner and Loewe, Frank Loesser, Irving Berlin and more!  
  
Cost:** FREE or Suggested Donation of $10 per person to offset costs. (Bill My Account is only open to Shomrei Members)

 About Bonnie Rapp**  
Bonnie had the honor of performing the lead role of Christine Daaé in the National Tour/San Francisco Company of Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera. Some of Bonnie’s favorite roles include Maria in The Sound of Music, Kate in Kiss Me, Kate, Cinderella in Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella, Louise in Gypsy and Sister Amnesia and Sister Leo in Nunsense, Nunsense II and Nunsense Jamboree. In addition, Bonnie has appeared in numerous galas, fundraisers, and Broadway concerts, including performances at Lincoln Center's Avery Fisher Hall.  
  
For the past decade, Bonnie has devoted her talents to providing live musical entertainment for a wide range of audiences, including corporate and community events, libraries, private celebrations, JCCs, and residents of independent living, assisted living, nursing homes, and memory care communities.

title: Christian & Jewish Singles Meet & Greet  -Online Zoom Event
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
Meet & Greet for Christian & Jewish Singles, ages 30 and over. This is an online event.

I asked Chat GPT some good questions to ask and we will be taking turns answering them. We will go through as many questions as we can in the limited time.

Chat GPT says:

### 🌿 Faith & Relationship with Values

* What role does your faith play in your daily life?
* What does a Christ-centered relationship mean to you?
* What qualities are most important to you in a partner?
* How do you usually grow spiritually?
* What’s something God has been teaching you recently?
* What kind of relationship do you hope to have one day?
* What are your biggest relationship values?
* What does healthy communication look like to you?
* What kind of family environment do you hope to build someday?
* What does commitment mean to you?

### 💛 Getting to Know Each Other

* What’s your favorite way to spend your weekends?
* What’s something people are usually surprised to learn about you?
* What’s a hobby or interest you wish you had more time for?
* What kind of personality are you naturally drawn to?
* Are you more introverted or extroverted?
* What’s your favorite worship song or Christian artist right now?
* What’s one thing that always makes you feel encouraged?
* What’s your favorite Bible verse and why?
* What kind of conversations do you enjoy most?
* What’s something you’re passionate about?

### 🤍 Deeper Dating Questions

* How do you handle conflict or disagreements?
* What boundaries are important to you while dating?
* What does spiritual leadership look like to you?
* How important is church involvement to you?
* What are you praying for in your future relationship?
* How do you balance grace and accountability?
* What kind of support helps you feel cared for?
* What are some lessons you’ve learned from past relationships?
* How do you stay grounded during difficult seasons?
* What are your long-term goals and hopes?

### 💍 Bible Study Questions

* What’s one prayer God has answered in your life?
* What Bible story inspires you most?
* What’s something you appreciate in Christian friendships?
* What does “loving like Jesus” look like in relationships?
* What’s one quality you admire in strong Christian couples?
* What’s something young Christians struggle with in dating today?
* How can relationships help people grow spiritually?
* What’s one piece of dating advice you think is underrated?
* What’s your favorite way to serve others?
* What helps you stay encouraged in your faith?

### 🌸 Fun Questions

* Beach or mountains?
* Worship night or game night?
* Sunrise or sunset?
* Texting or FaceTime?
* Sweet snacks or salty snacks?
* Road trip or staycation?
* Big group hangout or one-on-one time?
* Fancy dinner or casual café?
* Books or podcasts?

### 📖 Fun but Meaningful

* Which person in the Bible do you relate to most and why?
* If you could ask God one question right now, what would it be?
* What does your “dream life” look like if God is at the center?

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:
Live African music and drumming events in NJ
6,7&8pm Issyra Gallery presents - Inspiration Trap Creativity workshop

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

Issa =2
Issa Sow is a contemporary international autodidact artist known as Issa=2.
He believes in life being a journey of continual growth with each new

title: Simple Sitting Meditation
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Christian Singles Meet & Greet  -Online Zoom Event
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
Meet & Greet for Christian Singles, ages 25-45. This is an online event.

I asked Chat GPT some good questions to ask and we will be taking turns answering them. We will go through as many questions as we can in the limited time.

Chat GPT says:

### 🌿 Faith & Relationship with Values

* What role does your faith play in your daily life?
* What does a Christ-centered relationship mean to you?
* What qualities are most important to you in a partner?
* How do you usually grow spiritually?
* What’s something God has been teaching you recently?
* What kind of relationship do you hope to have one day?
* What are your biggest relationship values?
* What does healthy communication look like to you?
* What kind of family environment do you hope to build someday?
* What does commitment mean to you?

### 💛 Getting to Know Each Other

* What’s your favorite way to spend your weekends?
* What’s something people are usually surprised to learn about you?
* What’s a hobby or interest you wish you had more time for?
* What kind of personality are you naturally drawn to?
* Are you more introverted or extroverted?
* What’s your favorite worship song or Christian artist right now?
* What’s one thing that always makes you feel encouraged?
* What’s your favorite Bible verse and why?
* What kind of conversations do you enjoy most?
* What’s something you’re passionate about?

### 🤍 Deeper Christian Dating Questions

* How do you handle conflict or disagreements?
* What boundaries are important to you while dating?
* What does spiritual leadership look like to you?
* How important is church involvement to you?
* What are you praying for in your future relationship?
* How do you balance grace and accountability?
* What kind of support helps you feel cared for?
* What are some lessons you’ve learned from past relationships?
* How do you stay grounded during difficult seasons?
* What are your long-term goals and hopes?

### 💍 Bible Study Questions

* What’s one prayer God has answered in your life?
* What Bible story inspires you most?
* What’s something you appreciate in Christian friendships?
* What does “loving like Jesus” look like in relationships?
* What’s one quality you admire in strong Christian couples?
* What’s something young Christians struggle with in dating today?
* How can relationships help people grow spiritually?
* What’s one piece of dating advice you think is underrated?
* What’s your favorite way to serve others?
* What helps you stay encouraged in your faith?

### 🌸 Fun Questions

* Beach or mountains?
* Worship night or game night?
* Sunrise or sunset?
* Texting or FaceTime?
* Sweet snacks or salty snacks?
* Road trip or staycation?
* Big group hangout or one-on-one time?

* Books or podcasts?

### 📖 Fun but Meaningful

* Which person in the Bible do you relate to most and why?
* If you could ask God one question right now, what would it be?
* What does your “dream life” look like if God is at the center?

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
**IMPORTANT NOTE:** In order to prevent event cancellation I’m going to need at least one member who I’ve previously met and played with to confirm meeting at 8 AM via public comment. Not everyone is going to want to start this early but no one is going to want to hold a court by themselves for a half an hour or more. So when lacking this confirmation I’m going to cancel the event within an hour of the official start time. Either way, please use the comments to coordinate better start times for yourselves with others. We can’t please everyone with an exact start time but if we all communicate here then we can at least try. So please let us know your planned arrival time in the comments and be sure to monitor the event and discussion and be ready to adapt accordingly.

**VOTES:** Since this is still a “test” time slot, I welcome votes from proven members for changing the official start time. If we’ve already met then private message me your vote for the exact time and I’ll start an official record. Thanks for your patience and understanding as we work this all out.

**ABOUT THE GROUP:** We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition. We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Casual Volleyball - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We're a group of people who will start by hitting the ball around for the first 20-30 minutes and then will break up into 2-4 teams for two or three hours of play.

If we have more than 20 people show up, we'll break up into three or four teams of 6 (Some may have 7, 8 or 9. Additional players just rotate into play). Games will be to 10 points. Rally scoring. Winner stays on (unless a team has won four straight).

We'll be heading outdoors to the hard court in Leonia off Overpeck County Pk Driveway in the Overpeck County Park.

\*\*\ \*After playing, we'll be likely heading to Tropical Juice Bar, an idea of regular attendee Kate, for a drink and snack. It's located at 60 River St. in Hackensack. Feel free to join us or suggest another spot for a post-volleyball hangout. \*\*\*

There's no fee to play volleyball and nothing else you need to do besides show up. Come anytime!! All are welcome!!! We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form. We're more for people who haven't played in months, maybe years, and just want to occasionally play again and hang out.

Directions: You can Google "Volleyball Court in Leonia" and it should come up. Or type 41 Willow Tree Road, Leonia, NJ 07605 into your GPS, but note that it's not on Willow Tree Road, just near it. Instead, turn onto Overpeck County Pk Driveway off Fort Lee Road (Degraw Avenue). It is past the tennis courts and near a basketball court and track. You can try Googling Leonia High School as well. That should help you find it.

We don't have the court reserved and if it happens to be taken, we may play with those already occupying it or we will try to relocate on the fly. It's certainly possible that we may have to cancel that day if we can't find a suitable spot. Please keep that in mind. And if it's looking like it'll rain or snow, I'll make a call on whether to cancel around an hour ahead of time.

Please bring a ball and net if you have them for possible use during the game. Feel free to bring a speaker for music, or snacks and drinks for consumption during play.

If you have trouble finding the court or group, you can call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609. There is plenty of parking and an open bathroom at the park.

Hope you'll join us for our 19th official volleyball event. Questions or comments? You can message Andy on Meetup, or call/text him at 201-234-9609. Check out bowling, soccer, volleyball, tennis or one of our other activities at: www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - June meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
**IMPORTANT NOTE:** In order to prevent event cancellation I’m going to need at least one member who I’ve previously met and played with to confirm meeting at 8 AM via public comment. Not everyone is going to want to start this early but no one is going to want to hold a court by themselves for a half an hour or more. So when lacking this confirmation I’m going to cancel the event within an hour of the official start time. Either way, please use the comments to coordinate better start times for yourselves with others. We can’t please everyone with an exact start time but if we all communicate here then we can at least try. So please let us know your planned arrival time in the comments and be sure to monitor the event and discussion and be ready to adapt accordingly.

**VOTES:** Since this is still a “test” time slot, I welcome votes from proven members for changing the official start time. If we’ve already met then private message me your vote for the exact time and I’ll start an official record. Thanks for your patience and understanding as we work this all out.

**ABOUT THE GROUP:** We are typically beginner to intermediate levels playing in a friendly, sociable, and supportive environment while not being shy to a little friendly competition. We may rally freely in the beginning to warm up and then move on to some quick-rotation matches between 5-7 points. No formal teams here so everyone should be ready to both play with and against everyone else who shows up.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please be sure to bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. Also, I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own as well in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make serious plans to attend then please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Chester County Abandoned Rail Trace Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this interesting point to point hike tracing as close as we can to some of the more obscure abandoned railroad beds in Chester County PA!
Meet at the Uwchlan Trailhead on Dowlin Forge Road where it hits the Struble Trail. From here, we will shuttle with as few cars as possible north to the area fo Struble Lake.
We'll follow some pleasant back roads for a bit, first tracing some of the former Wilmington and Northern line.
From here, we'll head to the junction site at Supplee.
We'll continue down along a branch of the Brandywine Creek using various trails and parks, sometimes directly on the former New Holland Branch of the Pennsylvania Railroad, sometimes close to it on back roads.
We'll pass a great many former station sites.
There are quite a few little parks we'll pass through, and the back roads will be pretty nice as well.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Jazz film screening - Billy Bang: Lucky Man
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
In March 1967, BILLY BANG was conscripted to fight one year in the jungles of Vietnam, an experience that left him emotionally desolate and profoundly confused about his American identity. Upon his return, he tried to forget his nightmares through alcohol, drugs and music.

Forty years later, he decides that the only way to repair his emotions and find closure to his trauma was to return to Vietnam, this time with his violin.‍ Billy Bang: Lucky Man documents his brave return to the battlefields of his past, fraught with memories and flashbacks, in contrast to the ebullient and youthful Vietnam of today as he encountered a people and a culture that he had never known, and had been taught to hate.

Bang's journey takes him through the rich musical traditions of Vietnam, from Saigon and the Mekong Delta, north across the 17th parallel, climaxing with his collaboration with the Hanoi symphony orchestra.‍ Billy Bang: Lucky Man is about his desire to overcome and transcend the trauma of war through music and art.

________

“Billy Bang Lucky Man,' which documented Billy Bang's return to Vietnam, blew me away away. There were no punches pulled as we got to see this former GI - "a tunnel rat" - deal simultaneously with the people he once viewed and treated as the enemy while negotiating his own trauma and emotional turmoil. This film boldly documents the musical redemption, the journey to the light, that Billy Bang experienced as a result of that trip to the heart of darkness.”
Paul Bradshaw - Straight No Chaser

For adults with dementia and their caregivers, this event offers a welcoming, safe, calming space for socializing, music, art and reminiscing every month.


A “Memory Café” is a dementia-friendly social gathering for individuals with early-stage memory loss or mild cognitive decline and their care givers.

The meetings will be held in a safe and comfortable environment where people can interact and socialize with others having similar experiences. At the gatherings participants can get support in a non-judgmental setting, while enjoying the benefits of music for the brain.

The meetings will be run by Lisy Espindola, LCSW and Kim McLennon, MSW and music therapist. Lunch and/or snacks will be served.

This is a joint program between Lifelong Montclair at the Township of Montclair and the Montclair Public Library.

Attendance is free but registration is required. Questions? Call 973-744-3278.

title: Celebration: The Poetry of Nikki Giovanni, Audre Lorde, and Lucille Clifton NEW - In-Person
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
Join us for a celebration of the poetry of Nikki Giovanni, Audre Lorde, and Lucille Clifton— three critically acclaimed, beloved Black women poets. In accepting Lucille Clifton’s invitation in “won’t you celebrate with me,” we explore the beauty, resilience, wisdom, and triumph of their works. 

“Come Celebrate With Me” is a year-long series of programming honoring 100 years of observing Black history in America. Founded in 1926 by Carter G. Woodson, Negro History Week evolved into Black History Month, opening the door for additional annual commemorations such as Juneteenth, Black Music Month, Caribbean Heritage Month, Kwanzaa and more.

Montclair Public Library will honor the centennial of these commemorations in 2026 through a series of programs designed to engage and connect participants while highlighting and celebrating the experiences and contributions of people of African descent in the United States.

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

title: Bus Trip: Enjoy the New Studio Museum of Harlem, Soul Food Dinner and Gospel Concert
location: Montclair - Offsite, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Registration closes May 18. No refunds. We'll start out at the remarkable new Studio Museum of Harlem, a building faced in a series of black concrete frames that cost $160 million to create, taking a docent tour of two new exhibitions of exciting emerging artists. We'll also have a chance to explore the museum's other treasures on your own, including the gift shop.

We'll walk 5 blocks to an early soul food dinner at the United House of Prayer for All People Cafeteria, one of Harlem's hidden gems that has attracted headliners at the old Apollo Theater like Luther Vandross and Dionne Warwick, before enjoying a soulful gospel concert at the Convent Avenue Baptist Church. Then we'll return home.

title: RAG for Data Engineers: What It Is, Where It Fits, and Why Your Metadata
description:
Cloud Data Driven
Large language models are only as useful as the context you give them. For data engineers, that context is your schema, your lineage graph, your query history, your dbt models — and most teams haven't connected those dots yet.

This session is a practical introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation from a data engineering lens. We'll cover what RAG actually does under the hood, why it matters more for data teams than most, and the four places it shows up naturally in the data engineering workflow: answering schema questions without digging through a stale catalog,

Grounding SQL agents in your actual table definitions, giving incident response agents access to historical pipeline context, and surfacing institutional knowledge that currently lives only in senior engineers' heads.

title: Inspiration trap creativity workshop
description:

Only 10 attendees allowed social distancing and mandatory mask wearing.

You are invited to participate in a special session of creative thinking and fresh insight dedicated to inspiration.

We live in a world of constant change that requires us to be able to continually adapt and innovate in order to succeed. Unfortunately, many of us have forgotten how to delve into our raw creativity and leave behind the rigidity of the frameworks we have progressively interiorized.
This unique workshop seeks to reclaim our inspiration and imagination, rethink the unthinkable. It is ideal for people working in the creative arts as well as students, entrepreneurs, team managers, corporate leaders and anyone looking to implement their creative vision.

Inspiration is a vital driving force in our lives that moves us to create our best work and lights the way for new, authentic ideas. How do we invite, cultivate and harness inspiration so that we are able to bring these ideas into reality?
As a self-taught artist exploring various avenues of self-expression, Issa Sow draws a distinction between the phenomenon of inspiration itself and our task of making ourselves ready for it.
In the upcoming Inspiration Trap workshop, we will imagine ways we can invite and contain our inspiration, and well as keep our mind in the open, dynamic state as a receptacle or a “canvas” to collect, reflect and grow our ideas.
Feel free to bring along a personal object, a piece of clothing or even a small piece of furniture to play with during this hands-on experiment in innovative thinking. There are surprises and new elements in each session!

title: South Mountain Crest Trail
description:
Let's Walk!!
Let's Walk!! in South Mountain and visit Washington Rock and traverse a few of the many trails in the Reservation.

Washington Rock is Essex County Park System's bona fide Revolutionary War historic site, dating back to the late 1700's when Beacon Signal Station 9 was located here—one of 23 beacons built by General Washington to observe British troop movements quartered on Staten Island and New York City.

Seems like a great place to remember the nation's 250th birthday

This hike will be about 3-3.5 miles and mostly flat. The terrain is mostly dirt trails in the woods, so please wear sturdy hiking boots. **Bug spray and protective clothing is a good idea.**

Please arrive a few minutes early. We start promptly at the time posted. The hike should take us 60-90 minutes. **Please remember to bring water!**

Inclement weather may cancel this event. Please check the event page for comments prior to leaving for the meetup.

**Disclaimer:** If you join this event, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

title: Weekly Labyrinth Walks, Wednesdays 11am-1pm
description: Weekly: Wednesdays 11am-1pm in the Sanctuary  Take your soul for a walk on the labyrinth.  We are pleased to offer labyrinth walks each Wednesday in the mid-day as a chance to connect with your soul in our beautiful sanctuary. The labyrinth is an ancient spiritual tool , a mode of “walking prayer” that invites us to go deeper in our walk with God.  Our labyrinth, modeled on one in Chartes Cathedral in France, sits as the center of our Sanctuary, a constant metaphor for our spiritual lives.  Just like the labyrinth, our lives are not linear, but filled with twists and turns.  Sometimes we make great progress, and other times we feel we are going backwards.  But if we trust in the path we will find ourselves in the center -- the heart of God. All are welcome to take their souls out for a healing walk... no experience necessary!  Check out this lovely write up on Baristanet from the Spring 2014. Watch this video to find out more about walking the labyrinth. If you’ve never done so come out one Wednesday evening and give it a try. It is a wonderful way to nourish your soul and spend some quiet time in prayer or meditation.

description:

How do I sign-up?

Register online through Fusion, in the Student Recreation Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340).
Cost for Students $10;  $20 Faculty/Staff
Registration Opens on Fusion on Tuesday, May 26, 2026

Where and when?

June 29, 2026
10:00am –5:00pm
Begins at Student Recreation Center

What to bring: Water, lunch, weather appropriate clothing, boots (sneakers not acceptable), lunch, snacks, and sunscreen.
Potential Hazards: Unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, dehydration, allergic reactions/poisonous plants, insect bites and injury by running, including sprains, lacerations, abrasions and fractures.

title: 🥾 Let's Hike!! Jockey Hollow
description:
Let's Walk!!
Let's celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial (can you pronounce that?)

Come hike with us in the Morristown National Historic Park. We'll do about 3 miles along the Grand Parade loop, see a colonial era house and garden, and Revolutionary War soldier hut (replicas). It's a little like traveling back in time 250 years

[AllTrails: Grand Parade Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/new-jersey/grand-parade-trail?u=i&sh=vgtzxk)

**PLEASE NOTE THIS WALK IS AT 09:30**
**Please arrive 5 minutes early so we can start on time.**

We've scouted these trails and find them appropriate for most of our members. If you've walked with us at Eagle Rock, this is similar in difficulty with just a little more up and down. There may be wet or muddy sections and a few rocks and tree roots. Please wear hiking boots/shoes and bring trekking poles or a walking stick, if you prefer.

Don't forget your water!

Inclement weather may cancel this event. Please check the event page for comments prior to leaving for the meetup.

**Disclaimer:** If you join this event, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Help Desk - Bring Your Laptop, Yourself, and Your WordPress Problems
description:
WordPress Montclair Meetup
If you are running a WordPress site and are having issues and would like some help, then this Meetup is for you!

If you know some things, expert or not, and want to give back to the WordPress community, then this Meetup is for you too!

We will do our best to match a problem with a problem-solver. On-site and in real-time. Just bring yourself, your laptop, and your WordPress problems.

It's OK if you attend and only want to observe. We recognize this is how people learn. Given our time limit of two hours, we may not be able to solve everyone's issues, but we will try! If you are seeking help, please come prepared. Have your web site loaded in a browser, have your WordPress admin ready, along with a short list of issues you are trying to solve.

People helping are volunteers and may not be experts. There is risk to breaking your site! Please do not bring client or business sites that can impact reputations or revenue. If you have a staging site we can test things with, that is always preferred. If it is a production site, please create a site backup before having someone do any work on your site.

If you cannot find the group, please ask the front desk where the WordPress meetup group is meeting.

**PARKING**:
We've been asked to not park in the United Way lot behind the library as it could result in a parking ticket. Please find street parking or a parking deck.

\-\-\-
Join the **JerseyPress Slack** group to chat with others in our community and get help: [https://jerseypress.org/slack/](https://jerseypress.org/slack/)

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Meeting at the Verona inn!
description:
Board Game Night At Verona Inn
We will be doing our first monthly meeting starting on **February 25th at the Verona Inn!** We will be meeting up to organize games starting at 7:30, with food and drinks available courtesy of our host! You can play any game provided by hosts or bring your own! If you do not have a friend group to play games, hosts will organize you into pods with other people who need players. There are **no dues**. Future meetings will be held on the **last Wednesday of each month.**

More information and ground rules:

* **The doors open at 6:30 but games do not start until 7:30.** I *highly recommend* coming in during this period to eat your food and drink ahead of time!
* **Please return the graciousness provided by our hosts and order at least one item! All venue specific rules apply to our club.** Future meetings depend on treating our hosts with respect.
* **All games must be returned to their owners when they announce that they are leaving.** If you are in a game in progress when the meeting ends but it is not borrowed you may continue playing!
* **Please place food and drink on a separate table or surface from your games** to help avoid stains and other damage.
* **Please engage with others in good faith, sportsmanship, respect and common sense.** *ABSOLUTELY NO harassment, getting physical, hurtful insulting, and persecutory language will be tolerated.* Repeat violators of venue rules AND/OR this rule may be asked to leave the event and not return.
source: Meetup: Board Game Night at Verona Inn

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181
